articles.title: Preços 11.11: 47% dos produtos ficaram mais baratos, aponta g1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do g1 comparou preços de 74 produtos em lojas on-line nos dias 4 e 11 de novembro. Menos da metade ficou mais barata no cartão; 35% dos itens tiveram aumento de preço. Saiba quais.
articles.summary: Preços 11.11 caíram em 47% dos produtos avaliados, com descontos de até 65% no Pix para TVs e ar-condicionado, enquanto videogames mantêm os valores altos.
articles.body:
Menos da metade dos 74 produtos monitorados pelo Guia de Compras ficou mais barata no cartão de crédito durante o 11.11, data promocional realizada nesta quarta-feira (11).

🕵️O levantamento comparou os preços dos mesmos 74 produtos em lojas on-line nos dias 4 e 11 de novembro, para verificar quais ficaram mais baratos, mais caros ou mantiveram o valor na data promocional.

A pesquisa também considerou os preços para pagamentos via Pix.

Dos 74 itens pesquisados, 35 produtos (47,3% de toda a lista) registraram redução de preço no cartão. Com pagamento por Pix, os descontos chegaram a 64,9% dos itens. Do total:

35 produtos (47,3%) tiveram redução no preço parcelado;

13 produtos (17,6%) mantiveram o valor da semana anterior.

Com pagamento por Pix, os descontos chegaram a 64,9% dos itens.

Os setores de ar-condicionado (inverter e portátil) e de TVs de tela grande foram os que mais aderiram à data promocional.

Sete em cada dez aparelhos de ar-condicionado ficaram mais baratos no cartão de crédito. Nas smart TVs , a redução atingiu 66,7% dos modelos.

Os eletrodomésticos de grande porte (como geladeiras e lava-louças ) registraram as maiores quedas de preço em reais, com produtos chegando a ficar mais de R$ 1 mil mais baratos no parcelamento sem juros.

Na contramão, os consoles de videogame (como PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X) não registraram ofertas relevantes no parcelamento, mantendo-se em preços elevados.

Já a categoria de celulares teve um comportamento misto: embora sete modelos tenham registrado descontos relevantes, a média geral de preços do setor subiu 5%.

Isso ocorreu devido a reajustes isolados em modelos topo de linha em algumas lojas pesquisadas.

Veja abaixo o percentual de produtos que ficaram mais baratos no cartão de crédito em cada segmento analisado:

Ar-condicionado: 70% dos itens (desconto médio de 8,4% )

Smart TVs e TVs de tela grande: 66,7% dos itens (desconto médio de 8,2% )

Eletrodomésticos: 45,8% dos itens (desconto médio de 8,6% )

Celulares: 43,8% dos itens (desconto médio de 6,8% )

Eletroportáteis e Cozinha: 36,4% dos itens (desconto médio de 11,7% )

Videogames: 0% ( nenhum item com desconto )

A pesquisa de preços vem sendo feita semanalmente desde 27 de agosto e também nas "datas duplas" do período (9.9, 10.10 e agora 11.11). O resultado completo do monitoramento será publicado pelo g1 antes da Black Friday, em 27 de novembro.

VisionQuest is a Disney+ Original Miniseries centered around the character, Vision. The series is a spin-off from WandaVision and operates within the larger Marvel Cinematic Universe. Paul Bettany reprises his role as the character and is accompanies by James Spader, who plays Ultron.

As a Disney+ Original , VisionQuest is only available to watch via a Disney+ subscription . It's unlikely the show will make its way to any other services as long as Disney maintains the rights to Marvel, but it is likely it will eventually get a physical home release . Other Marvel TV shows , such as Loki and Wandavision, have gotten the Blu-ray treatment over the years.

VisionQuest is a miniseries consisting of only eight total episodes. The series release schedule includes batches of episodes until the final two episodes.

IGN reviewed episodes of VisionQuest based on the release schedule, combining multiple episodes at a time into single reviews. Our resident Marvel Comics expert, Jesse Schedeen scored each release as they arrive.

articles.title: Before the Storm Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Before the Storm is the second main quest of Skyrim, which automatically begins once you escape Helgen with your chosen accomplice, Hadvar or Ralof. Depending
articles.body:
Before the Storm is the second main quest of Skyrim , which automatically begins once you escape Helgen with your chosen accomplice, Hadvar or Ralof. Depending on who you went with, you can optionally speak to their family in Riverwood before meeting the Jarl of Whiterun to inform him of the dragon attack.

(Optional) Talk to Gerdur/Alvor in Riverwood

No matter who you emerge from Helgen with, your next destination lies in Riverwood , a town not far from here. Both companions have some relatives there that you can speak to and generously receive supplies from. Gerdur if you followed Ralof, or Alvor if you follow Hadvar.

Go to Riverwood and Meet Gerdur or Alvor (Optional)

En route to town, you can speak with your companion and learn more about the dragon and the background of his corresponding faction, at which point he attempts to -- albeit not forcibly -- recruit you to join the faction's collective cause. You can choose sides later; for now, continue to Riverwood.

Don't Miss: Guardian Stones stand just off the path as you head towards Riverwood -- they're hard to miss if you're following your companion. In this location, you will find the Rogue, Warrior, and Mage stones to receive a certain percentage boost in your learning speed, but you can only choose one.

Go with what your race and playstyle specializes in. For example, if you want to be a mage, pick the Mage Stone, which blesses the person with an accelerated learning of magic skills. Stealthy characters (like an archer) will want the Rogue Stone.

In Riverwood , seek out the person you are supposed to be following using the person marker on the compass - they're both near the main path through the town, near the main gate.

Either party is incredibly hospitable and will provide you with a number of respawning supplies free of charge. Take what you need (or take them all) and continue to probe the person of interest for any morsels of information. Eventually, the next task comes up: Talk to the Jarl in Whiterun , a sort of central location in all of Skyrim.

Nearby: Riverwood is worth exploring for a few side quests:

The Golden Claw : In the Riverwood Trader, Lucan is more than willing to offload one of his burdens upon you, tasking you with retrieving The Golden Claw. Of course, he rapidly assures that you will be rewarded for your efforts. This side quest overlaps with the next main quest, Bleak Falls Barrow , making it easy to complete it simultaneously.

A Lovely Letter: You can save or sabotage a burgeoning romance in the little town by speaking with Sven, a bard who frequents the Sleeping Giant Inn. There's an alchemy lab in the Sleeping Giant Inn that you are free to use as well.

When you're ready to set off for Whiterun, leave Riverwood and follow the quest marker northwards. Outside the periphery of Whiterun are a number of farms, stables, and a meadery that baulk at outsiders. You can see the high stone walls surrounding Whiterun.

When you reach the entrance, a guard stops you and tells you access to the city is limited to official business right now. Normally, you choose between persuasion , bribery , or intimidation , but in this case, you can simply inform the guard that Riverwood seeks aid. He lets you pass without a hitch.

Find Dragonsreach , the Jarl's keep on the hill in the northeast corner of town. There are boundless steps leading to it.

Any news of the dragon you may bring will win the Jarl's rapt attention. The quest ends as soon as the Jarl decides to dispatch help to Riverwood. You will then proceed to the Bleak Falls Barrow quest. If you've already been to this location as part of The Golden Claw side quest, then you'll have done the hard work already.

articles.title: Bleak Falls Barrow Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Bleak Falls Barrow is the third main quest of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, which sees you delving into a dungeon of the same name to retrieve the Dragonstone.
articles.body:
Bleak Falls Barrow is the third main quest of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , which sees you delving into a dungeon of the same name to retrieve the Dragonstone. While you're at it, you can also complete The Golden Claw side quest picked up from Lucan in Riverwood.

Use the links below to skip to key quest steps:

Retrieve the Dragonstone from Bleak Falls Barrow

Rewards: Word for the Unrelenting Force shout, enchanted leveled armor, and the ability to purchase Breezehome

Head toward the snowy mountains southwest of Whiterun, west of Riverwood, to soon encounter bandits and enemy archers. Go up to the peak of the mountain to find Bleak Falls Barrow, an old Nordic ruin. Enter the decrepit Bleak Falls Temple.

The interior is sparsely populated at the moment, but you'll find plenty of Skeever carcasses to pick at, as well as a locked chest on which to practice your lockpicking . After putting down the first two bandits , you won't encounter another until deeper in. Be sure to loot the burial urns for some Gold pieces and relieve the shelves of some potions as well.

Continue through the tunnels until you reach the puzzle room.

You reach a room with a lever and a gate. When you initially try to pull the lever, you will be met by a shower of arrows -- obviously this is an unintended result.

This mini-puzzle requires you to flip the three pillars on the left side to match the correct sequence of the pillars displayed above the gate. The pillar in the middle has fallen to the ground next to the lever.

The correct sequence is: snake, snake, fish . Pull the lever once you've set this pattern to open the gate.

Proceed to find a room with various loot, including a soul gem and a book. Reading the Thief book ahead improves your Lockpicking a bit.

Descend the spiral stairs to the cobweb-filled area below - be sure to pick up the Scroll of Fireball from the table after fighting the skeevers.

Hack through the thick wall of cobwebs and proceed to meet up with Arvel the Swift . You discover that this grandmaster thief has been captured by a Frostbite Spider, but managed to mortally wound and significantly weaken the giant arachnid. Finish it off and speak to Arvel. Before freeing him, inquire about the golden claw.

The double-crossing scum will try to run away, screwing you out of the claw. Kill Arvel and loot his body to take the golden claw.

You begin to head into the crypt, from which draugr emerge and attack. These are stronger foes than the bandits you have been seeing, so avoid dealing with too many at once.

Time the swinging axes and sprint through the corridor as soon as they retract. In these tighter spaces, you will encounter more draugrs, but notice that the slick, iridescent liquid on the ground -- it is flammable. Lure the draugrs over it and light it afire either with fire magic or knock one of the flame lanterns onto the oil.

One more Draugr pops out from the coffin; slay it and loot the chest for Gold and a Scroll of Hysteria .

Pull the chain nearby to access another part of the temple. This area is prime farming ground for Glowing Mushrooms , which can be harvested from the walls as you come to them.

The linear path leads outside to a small waterfall, the base of which features a chest and corpses to loot. The path eventually takes you to a restless draugr, a slightly sturdier variant that might require more effort to slay. The door ahead leads to Bleak Falls Sanctum. More draugrs, but there's also more oil to help you out.

Through the iron doors at the top of the stairs, you walk down the hall to the stone door ahead. On the stone door is a set of rings with symbols and a keyhole in the shape of the golden claw emblazoned on the door.

You can rotate each ring individually to match the engravings on the Golden Claw itself. Inspect the Golden Claw in the items menu to clearly see the correct order.

The solution, from the bottom, central ring to the top, largest ring is bear, moth, owl. Afterwards, put the Golden Claw in place to open the door.

Enter the large chamber and move towards the engravings on the Word Wall to learn Unrelenting Force , at which point a Draugr Overlord awakes.

Use the uneven terrain to your advantage; the Overlord has a hard time keeping up with you if you alternate between a high point and a low point, using a bow or long-range magic to deal damage.

Once you've killed the Overlord, loot the Dragonstone from its dead body.

You can then continue up the stairs and out through the cave opening, making your way back to the wilderness of Skyrim.

Now all you must do is return to Farengar in Whiterun. In his room, you will meet a mysterious woman named Delphine.

Farengar will take the Dragonstone from you, but you'll keep the Golden Claw, which you can return to Lucan in Riverwood to complete The Golden Claw quest.

Once you're done talking to Farengar, you will then proceed to the next quest, Dragon Rising .

articles.title: In the Heart of the Woods - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In the Heart of the Woods is a Side Quest that can be started in Fayrlund, a small village on the main island of Skellige. There's a key choice to make
articles.body:
In the Heart of the Woods is a Side Quest that can be started in Fayrlund, a small village on the main island of Skellige. There's a key choice to make during this Side Quest once you've started it, which will have a big impact on what you get as a Side Quest reward.

To help you make the best choice and get your reward quickly, here's IGN's complete guide to In the Heart of the Woods, including tips on the combat encounter. We've also included exclusive developer behind the scenes commentary about this Side Quest.

We reached out to the developers of Witcher 3 for their thoughts on their favorite quests and experiences! Paweł Sasko — Associate Game Director: " This quest is one of the oldest The Witcher 3 quests ever made — it was made by our Expert Quest Designer Joanna Radomska and myself, and we aimed to invent the new formula for quest design, a blueprint to replicate. But first we had a lot of questions to answer. What really enchanted me was the first time the forest started coming together, from foliage, to weather, wind, and the music, the shadows, the flock of crows moving through… This story captures one of the central ideas behind The Witcher, that sometimes there is simply no perfect answer. We always wanted players to leave quests discussing the decision they made instead of only talking about the combat. Both sides have understandable motivations, and the player has to decide which philosophy they believe in rather than which ending is objectively better.'"

This Side Quest can be looking for the notice that reads Contract: Woodland Spirit on the noticeboard in the Fayrlund area, or by overhearing the group of characters on the road to the south west of Fayrlund. There's a dead man in question here, who's been attacked by something in the woods.

To start, you'll need to investigate the marked areas in the woods using your Witcher Senses, following the clues to learn more about what might've killed the man being argued over, and then look at the Woodland Spirit entry in your Bestiary to continue the quest.

You'll need to make a decision on which one of two characters you want to listen to and proceed with. Sven wants to kill the creature, while Harald wants to leave it alone.

The best choice in In the Heart of the Woods is to accept Sven's offer who wants you to kill the Woodland Spirit (the younger man) and not the offer from Harald (the elderly man). If you go with Harald's offer you won't get to fight the Woodland Spirit and will miss this trophy!

If you do end up going with Harald, you'll need to accompany him to a woodland altar, defend said altar from five white wolves, then place their hearts on the altar.

You'll then need to speak to Harald in Fayrlund and then choose whether to protect him from the other characters or not -- if you choose to protect him, move quickly as the group can kill him quickly. You'll get your reward and wrap up the Side Quest here.

Working with Sven means tracking down the marked person to find the Leshen. To start, look for the crows at the last house on the left. The marked person will be Hilde, someone close to Sven, and you'll need to tell Sven, leading to the decision of whether to isolate her or kill her.

Your choice here doesn't matter a whole lot. When you have made a decision, head into the forest and use your Witcher Senses to find three totems. You need to destroy these totems, which will be guarded by wolves. Prioritize the totems over the wolves, then clear out the dogs.

The Woodland Spirit, a nasty Leshen, will then be ready to fight you nearby after a brief cutscene. It has a lot of health and will kill you in 1-2 hits. Always activate the Quen Sign to protect yourself from damage. The boss is quite slow though. Attack it quickly when it appears, so it doesn't get a chance to attack you first (and if it does your Quen Sign will protect you).

The key with Leshen fights is to light them up as much as possible, with Igni and Bombs. The Dancing Star Bomb can be particularly useful.

When the fight is over, you'll get 50 x experience and then need to head back to Fayrlund to speak to Harald. Turns out, while you were away, the elders were slaughtered.

The Side Quest will wrap up and you will get your reward.

Your rewards will vary based on what you picked. You'll always get 50 x experience and 60 x Crowns, but siding with Sven adds Assassin's Boots into the mix.

articles.title: King's Gambit - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: King's Gambit is a Skellige Side Quest with a suggested level of 18. It becomes available after helping Hjalmar and Cerys in side quests The Lord of
articles.body:
King's Gambit is a Skellige Side Quest with a suggested level of 18. It becomes available after helping Hjalmar and Cerys in side quests The Lord of Undvik and Possession . It's a rather lengthy Side Quest, but a very interesting one to take on if you're keen on learning more about the game's lore.

Here's IGN's complete guide to King's Gambit, including every crucial character interaction and how the Side Quest leads into the next one, Coronation.

After completing The Lord of Undvik and Possession, head back to Kaer Trolde to receive a reward from Crache. As you enter the main feast hall, a cutscene will occur where one of Crach's servants will greet Geralt and describe what is happening inside.

Once you get closer, you will see Cerys and Hjalmar arguing.

Afterwards, head to the Crach's room to find Berna leaving his room.

After talking a lengthy talk with Crach, there will be some loud shouting from the feast hall, and Geralt will run out to see that there are lots of Bears attacking people in the feast hall. Only three surviving potential members to be King/Queen will survive. Cerys, Hjalmar, and Svanrige Bran.

Crach is blamed for the Bears attacking members in the feast hall, and he and his son and daughter must find out how and why the attack happened. At this point, Cerys and Hjalmar both have different ideas on to how to deal with the issue at hand, and you can decide to help one of them.

You can help Cerys , or help Hjalmar . The best choice in King's Gambit is to help Cerys; you'll get slightly less experience, but you'll learn who was at the heart of the attack, finding the guilty party and securing a better ruler.

If you choose to help Cerys, you will stay in the room. Use your Witcher Senses to examine the bodies, and the bears. After examining the ear, there will be a more detailed examination on the head, torso, limbs. Geralt determines it was a human once, and something he ate or drank caused the transformation.

Use your Witcher Senses to examine the drinking apparatuses to find the cause of the contamination. Once you find it, follow the scent to the front of the room, behind the door, and to a small drinking glass. Geralt will call Cerys over, and she says to ask Hjort about the smell from the glass.

After talking to Hjort, Cerys thinks they drinks may have been tampered with in the cellars. Head to the cellars with Cerys. Once arriving in the cellar, head down the stairs, and examine the barrels ahead and to your right to find the barrel that was contaminated. As soon as this happened, someone throws a torch to burn and suffocate you and Cerys. Head towards Cerys, and there are a bunch of barrels blocking a passageway, break through using Aard , and continue following Cerys in the tunnel. You'll find a Quen sign place of power along the way.

You'll eventually arrive back in the keep, Geralt says he heard a something break before the fire started. Head back to the cellar door with Cerys to look around with witcher senses. There will be some mead, so follow the mead trail. When the trail breaks off , examine the nearby wall to find a piece of cloth. Cerys recognizes it as Armvald's tunic. As you get close to where he is, he rides away on horse.

Ride after him on your horse, when you get close swing at him with your sword to end the chase. After catching him, he will confess, and it was in fact Birna Bran who was the mastermind behind the attack.

There will be a cutscene with Cerys explaining to the rest that Berna Bran was the one at fault for the attacking. Armvald steps forth to say his proof. Geralt also steps forth to show the letters Berna sent to Armvald. Both of these are not enough proof to clear Clan an Crach. After, Berna Bran's son comes forth and accuses her mother. From this, they she is found guilty, and will be sentenced to death.

This will bring the Side Quest to a close, aside from a small interaction with Crach.

If you chose Hjalmar, you'll need to go to Fornharla, where you'll learn that the vidkaarls can turn into bears. The village is all but deserted, but there'll be an altar to a forbidden deity; forbidden because he required human sacrifice to be sated.

Use your Witcher Senses to follow the scent of incense from the altar, then follow the blood prints that the trail leads to. The trail will eventually take you to a house with a trap door that leads to a cave.

In said cave, you'll end up facing off against a vidkaarl who says that the group did not come to the feast to kill people. Hjalmar will join you in the fight, with the vidkaarl starting off as his regular self then turning into a bear, increasing his damage output.

Focus on your heavy attacks and dodging the quick attacks of the vidkaarl to get through this combat encounter. You won't need to protect Hjalmar heavily here, as he's fairly tanky.

You'll get 200 x experience for this combat encounter, along with a Berserker Hide and other goodies from the vidkaarl's corpse.

Moving further into the cavern, you'll need to disrupt a vidkaarl ritual here, with a Druid who declares that he won't tell you anything about the attack being quick to get rid of. He's squishy, despite his ability to summon bears, so focus on quick attacks.

Loot the Druid's body to reveal a letter that describes him being the advisor to the new King. You'll get 300 x experience, but won't know who was at the heart of the attack.

This will be the end of the Quest, aside from the following interaction with Crach that leads into the Coronation Quest.

Crach says there will be a Jarl's council and time to pick a King, and you can join him, or meet him later. The is the quest "Coronation" which is just a cutscene witnessing the person you chose to help become King/Queen.

Your final reward for this Side Quest is the Death from Above Crossbow and 400 x experience.

articles.title: Master of the Arena - The Witcher 3 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Master of the Arena is a Side Quest in The Witcher 3. It's a unique Side Quest where you'll need to intentionally lose a battle at one point to break
articles.body:
Master of the Arena is a Side Quest in The Witcher 3. It's a unique Side Quest where you'll need to intentionally lose a battle at one point to break a generational curse, letting Geralt get close to the brink of death to help a character called Ulle the Unlucky.

Here's IGN's complete guide to Master of the Arena, including the recommended level, where to find the Side Quest, and how to complete it easily.

This Level 14 Side Quest is available in Spikeroog. Go to the battle arena in the northwest of the isle and talk to the warriors on the walkway to learn about the ghost of a defeated warrior who is haunting the arena.

This ghost, Ulle the Unlucky, is doomed to always lose when he's battled in the arena. You need to face him to learn about his plight -- he'll challenge Geralt to a duel despite his curse.

To beat him, you have to actually lose. Don't worry, you don't have to die! Either keep blocking him attacks -- or just let him hurt you until you're almost dead and the end sequence of the quest will be triggered.

Once the curse is broken, head back to the warriors of the arena. They will promise to share a portion of their winnings with you.

Go back to the warriors to get paid once the quest marker indicates that the reward is ready to be picked up and the Side Quest will be marked complete.

Your reward will be given in chunks, but comes out to 35 x Crowns and 35 x experience.

VisionQuest is a miniseries, meaning there will only be a single season of episodes. The series kicked off on October 13 as two-episode premiere and will release weekly on Tuesdays in batches until the final two episodes.

All episodes will be available to stream with a Disney+ subscription as soon as they release. Seeing as the show is a Disney+ Original , it's unlikely you'll ever be able to watch the show without subscribing. Though there is hope that it will eventually get a 4K Blu-ray release .

IGN reviewed episodes of VisionQuest based on the release schedule, combining multiple episodes at a time into a single review. Our resident Marvel Comics expert, Jesse Schedeen scored each release as they arrived.

articles.title: VisionQuest Post-Credits Scene Just Confirmed A Major Marvel Character Is Coming Back in Upcoming Avengers Films
articles.summary: The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.
articles.body:
Spoilers for VisionQuest and potentially Avengers: Doomsday are contained in the article below. You've been warned!

The finale of VisionQuest confirmed that one of the most beloved characters from the MCU will be returning in the upcoming Avengers films, seemingly under the control of Doctor Doom.

Following the conclusion of VisionQuest, Marvel snuck in a little teaser for Avengers: Doomsday and/or Secret Wars during the credits. The scene was excluded from advanced screeners provided to the press, so it came as a big surprise and shows that Marvel made a great deal of effort to keep this moment a secret.

The show cut back to the ending of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, where Wanda Maximoff, AKA Scarlet Witch, uses her powers to destroy the Darkhold and, in the process, sacrifices herself. Her fate has remained unknown for over four years now, but now, we finally know what's next for her.

Doctor Doom shows up and lifts a bunch of rubble off of her, uttering the words: "Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine." Her eyes open in shock before the scene cuts to black. The plot of Avengers: Doomsday has remained relatively abstract for some time now. Universes are starting to catastrophically collide as part of a series of "incursions," but the why and how of it all has remained a secret. Doom's larger plan and motive have also been kept under wraps, but we've started to get a better idea over the last couple of months.

The post credit scene from the finale of VisionQuest! Well, Wanda’s back! — Spader Lover (Cosmic Muffin Lover) (@SpaderLoverGirl) November 11, 2026

The post credit scene from the finale of VisionQuest! Well, Wanda’s back!

At the end of the recent Avengers: Endgame re-release, we see Doom abduct the Hulk following the events of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . We also saw him try to make contact with a young Franklin Richards at the end of The Fantastic Four: First Steps, though it's unclear if he succeeded in taking him. We have yet to see the powerful child in any of the promo for Doomsday , so it's not out of the question that he has been recruited into some kind of dark army being built by Doom.

It's unclear what other characters may be in Doom's legion, but it's obvious that he's building up an absurdly dangerous level of power that will give the Avengers a run for their money. Many have been wondering how Marvel would top Thanos... and Doctor Doom creating an evil anti-Avengers roster could certainly be the answer. We don't have too much longer to go before we get more answers, as Avengers: Doomsday finally releases next month.

It won't be the end of this story, though. Avengers: Secret Wars is currently slated to release next December, though filming reportedly hasn't even begun... so a delay to 2028 may not be out of the question . Regardless, you can seemingly expect Scarlett Witch to appear in at least one of these projects, if not both.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Wild Oriole Sword - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Wild Oriole Sword is a one-handed weapon in Phantom Blade 0. It has a base damage of 295 and a base Guard Break of 104. It features a five-hit standard
articles.body:
The Wild Oriole Sword is a one-handed weapon in Phantom Blade 0. It has a base damage of 295 and a base Guard Break of 104. It features a five-hit standard combo and a three-hit Sha-Chi combo.

Oriole Song : Press L1+Triangle to consume Sha-Chi to enter the [Oriole Song] state for 10 seconds. While active, every Sha-Chi attack unleashes an air-rending blade wave as piercing as an Oriole's Song Wild

Oriole Sword Art : Pressing L2 consumes 1 Sha-Chi Essence to unleash the Wild Oriole Sword Art, assailing powerful enemies with an unrelenting flurry of sword strikes. This attack is unblockable.

How to Get The Wild Oriole Sword in Phantom Blade 0

In order to get the Wild Oriole Sword in Phantom Blade 0, you'll need to do two things. First, you'll need to find all five ribbons around the Village of Lu that pertain to Mu Xiaokui. After finding all five, you'll then need to finish the main story in the Village of Lu and fight the final boss, Mu Xiaokui, Young Mistress of the Order. Interacting with all five ribbons presents the secret third phase of the fight, and after defeating her, you'll be able to pick up the Wild Oriole Sword on the docks directly in front of you.

The Wild Oriole Sword can be upgraded to gain new buffs and abilities. Below you'll find a table that shows everything you can unlock.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Season 3’s First Four Episodes Accelerate Sauron’s War and Reenergize the Prime Video Series
articles.summary: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 prove a welcome return to Middle-earth, allowing the series to get back on track after two seasons of wandering.
articles.body:
Some spoilers for Episodes 1-4 of Season 3 and past seasons of The Rings of Power follow. Episodes 1-4 are available on Prime Video now, with Episodes 5 and 6 debuting on Nov. 18, and Episodes 7 and 8 finishing out the season on Nov. 25.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 is a new beginning for the Prime Video series, kicking the story off five years after where things ended in Season 2 , and streamlining the overall narrative into a more cohesive war story.

Season 3 refocuses The Rings of Power on its simple yet compelling good vs. evil premise, jettisoning some past characters and subplots while ensuring the ones remaining all align with the same goal: you exist to either defeat Sauron or to serve him.

Celebrimbor’s death last season means The Dark Lord (Charlie Vickers) isn’t having an easy time forging the One Ring. (Nice touch having Sauron keep Celebrimbor’s skeleton hanging around so his “ghost” – actor Charles Edwards returns for a cameo – can psychoanalyze him about his self-doubts.) Sauron desperately wants to discover whatever secret element Celebrimbor put into the Elven rings, as the Elves have thus far been able to stave off Sauron’s army at the borders of Lindon and Rivendell while nearly everywhere else in Middle-earth has fallen. To aid him in his quest to capture the Elven rings and discern their magic, Sauron has been busy turning mortal men into Nazgûl, promising them eternal life in exchange for becoming his servants of the ring.

Meanwhile, Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) have been busy battling the Orcs (and humans) that Sauron sends after them. Although she hasn’t encountered him in five years, Galadriel is beginning to feel Sauron’s presence again (Robert Aramayo’s Elrond thinks she’s just being paranoid). Galadriel’s past is briefly but sweetly explored here when she meets her future husband, Celeborn (a stalwart Jamie Campbell Bower , back to being a pretty boy following years of Vecna ugliness), during a flashback to the First Age, where they court each other in a wire-fu duel reminiscent of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon .

This sequence, when contrasted with the hardened warrior Galadriel has become, reveals how much she’s changed over a thousand years and the toll the conflict has taken on her. Morfydd Clark’s nuanced performance adeptly captures Galadriel's evolution from romantic to badass in just a few moments of screen time.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Photos

While the ongoing conflict between Sauron and the Elves is the main focus of Season 3, the first four episodes also catch viewers up with the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm, led by now-King Durin IV (Owain Arthur). While there’s some strained humor with the Dwarves, things get interesting with the arrival of Durin’s older brother, Thrain (the always compelling Eddie Marsan, who, even under a mound of makeup, proves an intriguing screen presence). Thrain has an agenda of his own that, by Episode 304, pits brother against brother for control of the dwarf kingdom. Durin and Disa’s (Sophia Nomvete) marriage is put to the test when a misstep from her past comes up, resulting in one of the strongest and most emotional scenes between the two in the whole series thus far.

In addition to Celeborn and Thrain, Season 3 also introduces another curious new addition to the cast in Marnûkh (Adam Young), the “orc with the arc” who initially seems like a willing soldier of Sauron’s but ends up having a more complicated role to play. Marnûkh’s presence puts Galadriel and Arondir’s feelings about Orcs to the test, ultimately leading to tragedy by the end of Episode 304.

Speaking of which, Season 3 also gives Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin), who has not always proved the most interesting character in this show, an Anakin-style arc. A grown man now, Theo has been enslaved by the Númenoreans the last five years, so when a chance presents itself for him to rebel against them – even if it means possibly becoming a Ringwraith for Sauron – he seizes it. This pays off hints that Theo was meant for the dark side that were first seeded in Season 1 when he found that broken sword hilt bearing the sigil of Sauron. He’s a bad guy now but, as with Anakin Skywalker, perhaps redemption is still possible for Theo in the end.

David Weyman’s Gandalf has more of the qualities we associate with the lovable wizard this season, and by Episode 4 his backstory and connection to Ciarán Hinds’ Dark Wizard is revealed (thanks to a Moses-like chat with The Sacred Fire), setting up a more interesting challenge for Gandalf than simply having to battle a fellow sorcerer. I’ll be interested to see how that plays out in the remaining quartet of episodes.

I found the Númenor storyline less compelling than the other plot threads explored in Season 3’s first four episodes, but that’s been my least favorite storyline of the series since Season 1. Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) is a political creature and he has always struck me as a player better suited for a historical drama about intrigue at the royal court than in this particular fantasy tale. He’s a Westeros power player dropped into Middle-earth and whenever the story dwells too long in Númenor, I yearn for it to get back to literally any other character’s plot line.

That said, Ema Horvath’s Eärien gets a key episode this season that realigns her with her father Elendil (Lloyd Owen) and brothers Isildur (Maxim Baldry) and Anárion’s (Andrew Richardson) cause. Given how she broke with them at the end of Season 2, how and why Eärien is now working as their spy goes unexplored (for now). Was that always the case and she was on a long-term undercover mission? Or did she finally see the light after being married to Pharazôn? That remains unclear to me.

And while the first four episodes of Season 3 still offer their share of action (sword fights, arrows, etc.), any grand-scale battles are apparently being held for later in the season once Sauron’s quest to forge the One Ring inches him closer to victory. With the latest trailer teasing a Balrog battle and Sauron wearing the One Ring , I fully expect the latter half of Season 3 to start ramping up the action to epic levels.

articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has broken a sale records for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game over its first four days of availability.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has broken sales records for Nintendo, and become the fastest-selling Switch 2 game over its first four days of availability.

Nintendo has already shifted 5.2 million copies of its newly-launched Zelda remake, the company announced today in a celebratory press release.

That means Zelda is selling faster than other notable Switch 2 arrivals such as Donkey Kong Bananza, Pokémon Pokopia and even Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the console last year. (Nintendo sold 3.5 million Switch 2 consoles over its first four days, with roughly 80% of those consoles sold in a bundle with Mario Kart World, at least in the U.S.)

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is Nintendo's big Switch 2 game for the holidays, so the firm will likely be pleased by its strong launch. It is one of the few other titles (hello, Barbie!) braving a November release, just a few weeks clear of this year (and decade)'s hugely-hyped arrival of Grand Theft Auto 6. But perhaps the firm has been wise to bet on Ocarina of Time's legendary status and broad audience being distinct enough to survive GTA's gravitational pull.

Originally released for the N64 back in 1998, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remains one of the highest-rated and most beloved games of all time. articles.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
articles.summary: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.
articles.body:
Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork taken from Super Mario 64.

Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS.

Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered.

"Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer . "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing.

"But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

While some fans might feel like it's a shame to see this more carefree attitude to Easter eggs is gone, it's fair to point out that Mario 64 Easter eggs (or Skyward Sword ones, for that matter) would make less sense today. Mario 64 was launched on the same platform as Ocarina of Time, of course, while Skyward Sword was released contemporaneously with the game's 3DS port. (Maybe Switch 2 just needs a new Mario game to actually arrive?)

60 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Screenshots

"I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game," Aonuma continued, "and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that... [But] you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way."

"No hard feelings there," commented Skyward Sword director Hidemaro Fujibayashi, who returned as a producer for this remake.

And one Mario reference does still survive via Talon — a character who is an obvious nod to Mario with his bushy moustache, plus red and blue overalls. Check out his necklace, and you'll see his golden Bowser charm remains intact, all these years later.

Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has previously discussed the idea of the company's different franchises crossing over , and said that he wasn't a fan — except when it is Pikmin , which he wants to include wherever possible.

Earlier today, Nintendo revealed that Ocarina of Time had already shifted 5.2 million copies and become the Switch 2's fastest-selling game so far. Meanwhile, players have been having fun in-game by performing everything from Linkin Park to the Titanic theme on ocarina .

The Taper Man: A Novel of John Le Carré's Circus

Each month we’ve been sharing the new books that you won’t want to miss , which should give you plenty of inspiration, whether you solely read sci-fi and fantasy or want to switch things up with a spot of horror, mystery thrillers, romance and romantasy or young adult.

But, these are the best books to have on your radar this month…

Release date: November 3 in the UK / December 8 in the US

If you’ve not already discovered Jason Pargin’s fantastic John Dies at the End series , now is the perfect time to acquaint yourself, with the fifth book being released early this month. It opens in a secluded small town, where a massive, sticky pile of severed human limbs have suddenly appeared in the parking lot of a vacant department store. And, if that wasn’t bizarre enough, a single set of footprints have been found in the snow, leading away from the pile.

Once it becomes apparent that there have been no reports of missing bodies, or body parts for that matter, things take an even stranger turn when some of the fingerprints of the severed arms are found to belong to living people, who happen to have all of their appendages intact. While others match no one on file, and the rest somehow have no prints at all. Basically, this sounds like a case for John, David (whose own arm, that’s still attached to his body, is found on the pile), and Amy. Running through December 28, both Amazon Prime and non-Prime members can sign up for three months of Audible Standard for $0.99 per month. In addition to the discounted membership, you also get an extra $20 in Audible credit.

Dangerous Impulses by Jennifer Lynn Barnes

We know that some of us can be put off by YA books, but if there’s one YA series that you need to add to your TBR list, it’s Jennifer Lynn Barnes’ bestselling The Naturals books. Basically, think Criminal Minds but with the characters being teens who have been recruited to the FBI’s classified youth program.

Picking up eight months after the events of the fourth book, Cassie, Dean, Michael, Lia and Sloane are turning their talents to a new endeavour. I mean, how difficult could it be to bring their FBI mentors back together? Especially when you consider the cases that they’ve dealt with up until now, as well as the serial killers that they’ve outsmarted and brought to justice. Well, it turns out that things aren’t quite as simple when it comes to Special Agent Veronica Sterling and her past. At the same time, it appears that an UNSUB committing crimes out in the snow is causing a cold case to become very hot, making it a Christmas that none of them will forget in a hurry.

With an epic story inspired by Slavic mythology, The Wolves of War definitely piqued our interest this month. Following Ivan and his daughter Halia, a girl who has been trapped in her own body since birth, could her newly awakening powers be the key to her and her family surviving what’s to come?

With two princes squaring off against one another and the threat of an iron-toothed witch haunting the shadows, now is the time for Halia to not only summon but master her magic to protect herself and her loved ones. But, in doing so, she must come to terms with a terrifying truth.

If you’re looking for a fun, escapist read this November, look no further than Cello's Gate by Maurice Africh. Who can say no to some sky pirates? It’s safe to say that Captain Grey and his crew have garnered quite a reputation for themselves, as the one squad who can accomplish the impossible. That is, until now.

When Dalia, the immortal daughter of the infamous ArchGovernor, asks them to find and steal the Stones of Indigo, it might seem like a relatively simple task. However, the stones don’t actually exist, at least not in the literal sense. They’re a myth and yet the allure of receiving one million credits per crew member, per stone, if they do find them, is too tempting for them to say no. Sure, Grey has never trusted the immortals and Dalia is definitely hiding something. What could go wrong?

Many of us will know Rebecca Yarros from her record-breaking The Empyrean Series of books, but she’s also a beloved romance author. And Peculiar Stars truly plays to her strengths in crafting a romance that we don’t want to put down.

It’s been relatively smooth sailing for Callista up until this point. That is until a routine trip to celebrate her engagement goes off course. Finding herself stranded on an island, alongside the crew and her fiancé’s cousin, Callista finally has a chance to question the life she always thought that she wanted. A slow burn kind of romance, when they are eventually rescued, the lives that they left behind might not necessarily have changed, but they certainly have.

When They Find Me: A Novel by Carter Wilson

For those of us who love a good mystery thriller, Carter Wilson’s latest release is ready to transport us to one of the most remote spots in America, somewhere that Annie has chosen as a safe haven for her and her daughter. With a population of just 313, Expanse, Colorado barely exists on a map. And given that the people looking for her aren’t the kind to forgive, or forget, this could be exactly the kind of place to keep them hidden.

Riven has been raised to survive in even the most inhospitable of circumstances. So, when her father leads them to the seemingly forgotten and isolated town of Expanse, in a bid to track down the man who apparently destroyed their lives, she knows what to do – strike fast, get revenge and then disappear. But, when the two women’s lives collide, things don’t exactly go as planned. What is the real truth? And who is actually to blame? We can’t wait to find out.

Given that Danielle L. Jensen has provided us with some of our favourite fantasy books over the past few years, we can’t wait to pick up her latest book, Defy the Dusk. And this new story – the first in a duology – follows Lirien as we discover the repercussions of her magic being unleashed two decades ago.

While the strongest survivors boarded the Dawnrider rig all those years ago, the rest of humanity was left behind. It was then that a king stepped forward to lead them through the turbulent times. Yes, Lirien was one of the lucky ones to find herself allowed on Dawnrider, but she’s also been looking for ways to overthrow the tyrant who is currently in charge of the rig. So, you can imagine her surprise when just as she’s getting ready to take her shot, she is abducted by the king. Offering her only two choices – help him and his people fight the creatures that she summoned in the first place, or be fed to them – the two enter into an unlikely alliance, with her magic being pushed to its very limits.

The Taper Man: A Novel of John Le Carré's Circus by Nick Harkaway

Fans of John le Carré’s most cherished character, George Smiley, will be happy to see the iconic spy return once more at the hands of fellow British author, Nick Harkaway. Set in 1965, in the midst of the Cold War, The Taper Man follows Smiley somewhere he’s never found himself before – across the pond in Los Angeles.

Could there be a traitor at the very top of the US intelligence agency? Well, with a Communist sleeper agent – the ‘Taper Man’ – poised to expose what Britain is getting up to in Moscow, it’s up to Smiley to find him. At the same time, his spy back in Leningrad is hunting down a Russian defector who could hold the piece to the puzzle they’ve been looking for.

Release date: November 3 (US) and November 5 (UK)

Now, we don’t know about you, but even though we probably shouldn’t be judging books by their covers, it’s tricky not to get sucked in by the looks of John Scalzi’s Monsters of Ohio. And this time, the author of the brilliant The Kaiju Preservation Society , brings us a tale of a town on the threat of literal extinction, with a few unexpected tentacles to boot.

Taking place in the sleepy pastoral community of Richland, Ohio, the town's inhabitants aren’t going to take it lying down, after a predatory private equity firm defrauded the area’s factory. However, what takes place might just be more than anyone bargained for. In fact, could it change humanity forever? You’ll need to pick up a copy to find out.

Ellis is a freelance journalist, based in the UK, with a love of all things books. She also routinely chairs bookish events up and down the country, getting the scoop from some of the biggest and bestselling authors to keep you in the know.

articles.title: Avengers Endgame: Encore Finally Gets a Disney+ Release Date, And It's Real Soon
articles.summary: Avengers Endgame: Encore will get an imminent Disney+ launch, it's been confirmed.
articles.body:
Avengers Endgame: Encore will get an imminent Disney+ launch, it's been confirmed.

The updated and extended version of Avengers Endgame will premiere via Disney+ as soon as this week, on Friday, November 13. That's according to an official listing now visible to subscribers in the U.S.

While a Disney+ arrival for Endgame's re-release always seemed likely, Marvel had held off providing official confirmation — likely to drum up more FOMO for audiences to watch in theaters. Indeed, the company also kept exact details of how it had extended Endgame under wraps until the film's cinematic debut in September — at which point its new scenes promptly leaked online .

Of course, fans have been able to watch Avengers Endgame via Disney's streaming service for years. But the Encore version is technically new, with fresh color grading and a series of additional sequences shot during the production of this year's Avengers: Doomsday.

Encore's most notable change to the original film is its extended version of Endgame's final scene, which previously concluded with Steve Rogers and Peggy Carters getting an uninterrupted happy ending. In Encore, however, this finale is abruptly halted by the arrival of Loki — seemingly from his time working as a TVA agent.

Other new scenes follow in fresh mid-credits and post-credits additions. This includes a found footage-style scene featuring Bruce Banner, set after his appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and a scene set within the TVA featuring numerous characters from the Loki series.

Finally, the movie now concludes with the original hammering of metal — previously a callback to Tony Stark forging the Iron Man mask — revealed to be Doctor Doom forging his own appearance. It's a neat tease for any future similarities between the two characters played by Robert Downey Jr.

Of course, these elements have all been added to tease the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday — and position that film primarily as an Endgame sequel rather than what it also is: the beginning of the end for Marvel's divisive Multiverse Saga.

With Avengers: Doomsday now just over a month away, the time feels right for Avengers Endgame: Encore to hit Disney+. It'll also arrive just days after another huge Doomsday tease arrived on Disney+ this week via a shocking post-credits scene in the finale of Vision Quest (beware spoilers!)

articles.title: This Is Where the Rings Are in Rings of Power Season 3
articles.summary: Where in Middle-earth are the Rings of Power as Season 3 begins, what does Sauron want with them, and what do they have to do with the One Ring?
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for Episodes 1-4 of Season 3 of The Rings of Power , which are streaming now on Prime Video.

Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power returns with the Tolkien timeline jumping five years and the balance in Middle-earth having tilted heavily in favor of the Dark Lord Sauron (Charlie Vickers). The brutal war has Sauron’s Orc armies decimating everything in their path — men are falling in droves, and even the Elves are taking a beating. But Sauron’s ultimate success is contingent on him forging the One Ring that will allow him to control all the Rings of Power.

For most of Season 2 , Sauron set up shop in Eregion pretending to be Annatar, the Elven "Lord of Gifts,” who offered his assistance to Elven Master Smith Celebrimbor (Charles Edwards). Together, they forged the separate Rings of Power sets — seven meant for dwarves and nine for men. Secretly, Sauron corrupted the dwarven rings delivered to King Durin III (Peter Mullan) to protect the realm of Khazad-dûm. And by the time Celebrimbor completed the nine rings for men, he realized far too late that Annatar/Sauron had been manipulating him and corrupting his creations. The horrified smith was murdered for his hubris, and Sauron took possession of the nine.

Which begs the question - where are the Rings of Power at the start of this season, and what is Sauron’s plan to use them to gain ultimate power over Middle-earth? Let’s delve in…

In the second season finale, Sauron stabbed Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) to take back the nine rings she meant to secret out of Eregion. In the five years since, Sauron has watched the weakening of men from Mordor as their armies fall or retreat in terror from his relentless swarm of Orcs .

Seeking to exploit their fear, Sauron devises a plan for the nine rings to accelerate his complete control over men. With the help of the Orcs, he collects small packs of starving, wounded or terrified men to become his Ring Servants, the Nazgnagôl — an early version of the eventual Ringwraiths. The men are commanded to battle one another to the death, with the victor winning Sauron’s tainted prize — one of the nine rings, its powers, and unequivocal loyalty to Sauron’s every command.

After the seven rings were delivered to Durin III, the king placed one on his finger and was instantly corrupted by unquenchable greed. It in turn incited his mania to mine deeper for the mithril ore which awakened the fiery Balrog which would become the agent of his demise. Durin IV (Owain Arthur) is crowned king, and one of the first decisions he makes with his wife Disa (Sophia Nomvete) is to hide the rings in Khazad-dûm so they don’t corrupt any more of their people.

But Sauron wants those seven rings, so he finds an exploitable mole from within — Thrain (Eddie Marsan), the eldest son of Durin III. The prodigal eldest son returns to Khazad-dûm, overthrows Durin IV, takes the crown, and hands the rings over to Sauron, meaning 16 of the Rings of Power are now in the Dark Lord’s direct control.

The only rings not to be forged with Sauron’s corruption in Eregion are the three Elven rings which bestow protection and healing through their wearer. By the end of Season 2, the ring Narya is worn by Círdan (Ben Daniels), Nenya is worn by Galadriel, and Vilya is worn by the High King Gil-galad (Benjamin Walker), who commands the Elven armies from Lindon.

Sauron is desperate to gain possession of at least one of the three Elven rings, believing that they protect Lindon and Rivendell from his armies. He also believes an Elven ring will aid in his creation of the One Ring which only Celebrimbor knew the secrets of how to forge. Sauron sends out the Nazgnagôl, who wear the rings of men, into Middle-earth on a mission to find Galadriel and retrieve her ring.

The forging of the One Ring is Sauron’s obsession, but he foolishly murdered Celebrimbor, and with him his centuries of singular smithing knowledge. (He stupidly had his notes burned as well.) All Sauron knows for certain is that the One Ring must be created in the fires of Mount Doom, so he spends his days chasing down any and all leads that will allow him to craft the ring that will bring Middle-earth to its knees under his rule.

Be sure to keep it locked to IGN for all of our Rings of Power Season 3 coverage in the coming weeks!

articles.title: What New DC Studios Boss Jeremy Latcham’s Past Comments and Films Suggest About the Future of the DCU
articles.summary: Outgoing DC Studios boss James Gunn and incoming boss Jeremy Latcham worked together on Guardians of the Galaxy. In fact, Latcham was the creative exec who hired Gunn to write and direct his first MCU film.
articles.body:
Once I absorbed the shock of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exit from DC Studios – I’d literally just interviewed Safran about DC’s future film and TV slate two weeks ago – I started researching Jeremy Latcham , the incoming President and Chief Creative Officer of DC Studios.

I’m sure my path must have crossed with Latcham’s in the past either during his stint at Marvel Studios or when he served as a producer on Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves or Bad Times at the El Royale .

Who Is New DC Studios Boss Jeremy Latcham?

Latcham started at Marvel in 2004 when Avi Arad still ran the show and Kevin Feige was a top deputy. Latcham eventually rose to become Marvel’s Senior Vice President of Production and Development.

He served as an associate producer on Iron Man, a co-producer on Iron Man 2, and an executive producer on The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, Avengers: Age of Ultron, and Spider-Man: Homecoming. That 2017 film was Latcham’s final Marvel project, when he left for an overall production deal with 20th Century Studios .

Gunn and Latcham worked together on Guardians of the Galaxy . Indeed, by Gunn’s own admission, Latcham was the creative exec who hired him to write and direct his first MCU film. Watch this resurfaced clip below of Gunn and Latcham on the red carpet for Guardians recounting how they began working together.

Also: It's worth pointing out that Jeremy Latcham was one of the guys that hired James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy. In fact, he was the one that interviewed him for the job. So yes, I do think he still wants him as a creative in DC Studios. — Lee Pace should be Batman. (@WayneG1939) November 9, 2026

Also: It's worth pointing out that Jeremy Latcham was one of the guys that hired James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy. In fact, he was the one that interviewed him for the job. So yes, I do think he still wants him as a creative in DC Studios.

But it’s the work that Latcham has done after Marvel and Hasbro (where he once had an overall deal to produce movies based on their IP) that has now gained some attention to his hiring on social media, including Latcham’s appearance on the Bible Bros podcast earlier this year.

A proud Christian, Latcham recalled on that show how his faith shaped his values, the movies he wants to make, and the stories he finds most worth telling. These insights may shed some light on what to expect from his stewardship of DC Studios, which is now owned by David Ellison’s Skydance.

While Ellison’s personal political views are somewhat murky – he claims to have supported both Republican and Democrat candidates in the past – his business dealings with the current Trump Administration in pushing through the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger , and his locking horns with Democratic state attorneys general who had hoped to block the deal, certainly made him appear aligned with Trump’s particular brand of conservatism.

Wouldn’t Ellison then want someone at the helm of DC Studios whose perceived values and politics align more closely with his own and who would produce DC content that’s reflective of those values? Gunn’s anti-Trump views are well known and as much as he tried to couch his Superman film as being about embracing hope and compassion, it’s almost impossible not to view that movie as a repudiation of the meanness and cruelty that have marked the current administration’s policies.

One might think Latcham, an exec who has worked for the faith-based and family entertainment company Wonder Project , might want to bring a more conservative or family-first leaning to the DCU than the more progressive bent that’s marked Gunn’s projects. That’s entirely possible but it’s not like religion or faith in general was absent from Gunn’s films. While Gunn has previously said he is “anti-religion” in the organized sense, he elaborated on his feelings about religion in an interview back in 2014:

“My personal take is that there is a role for spirituality in some people’s lives and I think that a belief in God can be a good thing for a great amount of people,” said Gunn. “I do not like any sort of faith or religion that is based on exclusivity, meaning any sort of religion that says you’re damned to hell or you’re not going to be saved because you don’t believe the same thing I do. I believe faith and spiritual belief is a very, very personal thing and if I started applying what I believe to everybody else it would be unfair to everybody’s individuality and I really hate that.”

How Latcham's Faith Helped Inform the Early MCU

For the incoming DC Studios boss, Latcham told the Bible Bros how he helped contribute to Marvel’s Phase 1-2 films, including Gunn’s Guardians of the Galaxy, by pushing that they spoke to people like his grandparents by telling redemptive stories with heart.

“All those Marvel movies I worked on, the way the company worked and was structured, I was really the guy creatively on the ground with the filmmaker guiding the development of the movie and the story. And so for me, it was always looking for redemption in these characters and looking for ways for connection so that you could take something from the movie and bring it into your life,” Latcham told the podcast.

“I've never been interested in just making an action movie,” he continues. “To me, it's like the reason a movie would stick around with you is because of the characters and because you see them overcoming flaws and becoming better people and redeeming themselves, or growing or learning or something. And so that was super important on all those films, was just to instill a sense of heart. And so it wasn't instilling faith, per se, but it was instilling redemptive qualities into these characters and seeing the growth that they could have and seeing how that could be relatable to your own life.”

A member of the Made for Texas advisory council , Latcham cited Guardians of the Galaxy’s Peter Quill as an example of a character seeking redemption. He said that although Guardians of the Galaxy isn’t “overtly a faith story or anything” that “you see this guy learn and grow so much in this beautiful journey, from a guy who can't take his mother's hand as she's dying at the beginning of the story to uniting his friends and holding their hands and finding community and putting his faith in people and growing together in a beautiful way. It's something nice there. ... My thing is always heart, humor, spectacle, in that order. That's my thing that I say over and over 1000 times on a movie, people make fun of me for, because I'm always like, ‘Do we care? Is there heart? Are we laughing along the way?’ And obviously you need spectacle because it's a movie, but heart's really what I care about when we're developing a film.”

Latcham also explained how he pushed for a redemptive arc to be “a guiding light” in the first Iron Man because he wanted the film to appeal to Midwestern viewers like his grandparents:

“I remember my grandmother called me when Iron Man 1 came out and she said, ‘Our pastor on Sunday preached about the movie and he doesn't even know that you worked on it. The restorative redemption wove its way into his sermon and Iron Man was the proxy for redemption that he used as trying to make yourself a better person.’ And I was like, ‘Oh, man.’ All the time that [Iron Man director Jon] Favreau would joke and be like, ‘Oh, Jeremy's Meemaw and Peepaw wouldn't like this.’ It ended up [that] the movie connected and was for Meemaw and Peepaw at the end of the day. … And that was a guiding light for how we made stuff in those early days of Marvel, was wanting to connect and feel redemptive and feel hopeful and feel like it had something to say that was meaningful.”

What Latcham's Views Suggest About the Future of DC Studios

That emphasis on redemptive story arcs with a hopeful bent isn’t at odds with what James Gunn had already brought to the DCU. After all, no one in the DCU has a bigger redemption arc than Chris Smith, aka Peacemaker. But that’s also where one could expect to see Jeremy Latcham’s DCU wildly differing from Gunn’s. I wouldn’t expect to see any more full frontal male nudity, orgies, drug use or even excessive profanity in the DCU that Latcham will oversee.

Elsewhere in the Bible Bros podcast, Latcham recalled how, when he was at the Wonder Project, the goal was to produce movies that embrace patriotism and pro-America messaging: “The core message there was faith in God, obviously, faith in country, faith in family, faith in fathers. Faith in all these institutions that we believe in in America: the idea of America, the idea of a democratic, free, capitalist society. All these things that we take for granted, that people are losing faith in on the daily like, ‘How do we make these things that we believe in front and center in these movies?’”

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

If Latcham doesn’t completely reboot the DCU it would seem likely that future DC projects might bring back “the American way” to the Superman character’s motto. Latcham, who was on that podcast to promote his Nate Bargatze-led film The Breadwinner , expressed his hope and desire to see the revival of genres like romantic comedies and G-rated live-action films, while also repeatedly expressing his disappointment in so much R-rated horror fare the industry has produced. (I guess fans shouldn’t hold their breath waiting for a Clayface sequel despite the R-rated horror film being a modest box office success for DC Studios.)

Latcham told the podcasters that his post-Breadwinner goal was to “build a slate of movies that are really diverse because I want to have healthy options when I go to the movie theater to see anything. I want to be able to see any different type of movie. I find it really frustrating when it's the same thing over and over again at the box office. So I'm trying to build movies that are all redemptive, that all have heart, that all give us a little something to think about, to do better, to grow, to learn, to try to make ourselves better in this project of being a human.”

Perhaps that’s the same goal he will bring to DC Studios. Maybe there is room within the DCU tent for G-rated fare or even some PG-rated superhero rom com. We’ll just have to wait and see what Jeremy Latcham has in store when he assumes command of DC Studios on December 1.

Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

articles.title: Mass Effect Could Still Be Saved, Ex-BioWare Developer Suggests, With Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Holding the Key
articles.summary: The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.
articles.body:
The future of Mass Effect could be secured with a key learning from the beloved Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, a former BioWare veteran has suggested.

In the days since EA announced it was shutting down its storied RPG game studio and killing its in-development Mass Effect Universe project, discussion has turned to the costs behind creating another AAA-budget entry in BioWare's space opera series, following a report that EA decided to invest in Star Wars instead .

Last week, BioWare co-founder Trent Oster suggested that EA would likely have been on the hook for at least $200 million in development costs to finish Mass Effect Universe at a level that fans expected.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200m+," Oster wrote on X/Twitter. "That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work." (To be fair, there is still that Mass Effect TV series in the works. And there certainly won't be any bigger plan in place for the IP if its flagship next game is cancelled.)

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

Now, Mass Effect lead programmer Christina Norman has said the game could be made for around $50 million — a figure that is five times the budget spent by the makers of Clair Obscur.

Highlighting a report on the French-made RPG's overall budget, which was pegged at less than $10 million, Norman wrote on X/Twitter that this was "a good example of why I think another Mass Effect game could be made for well under 200 million.

"I mean 5x the budget of Claire obscure expedition 33 should be more than enough," she continued. "You can always spend more but clever small teams can get it done."

Norman spent more than six years at BioWare working on the original Mass Effect trilogy, firstly as a lead programmer responsible for creating the franchise's conversation system, before moving on to become lead designer for Mass Effect 2 and 3, working to improve the series' gameplay.

In the years since, Norman served stints at Riot Games and her own co-founded startup, before becoming a full-time machine learning engineering consultant focused on LLM-directed character conversations. Still, there's no suggestion that LLM technology would be needed to turn in Mass Effect Universe on a smaller budget.

Even Oster has said he believed a new Mass Effect could be made for "cheaper" than $200m, though it "wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept," he wrote in a follow-up post. Alas, Oster also highlighted another big blocker to a new Mass Effect being made — that EA still owns the franchise's rights, and may never want to give them up, even if it's not actively using them. "The big push would be getting the IP free," he concluded. "The fans deserve more."

Last week's annual N7 Day celebration of the Mass Effect franchise featured the Normandy's cast and crew teaming up for a video message asking fans to help save Mass Effect . This followed an array of footage and details for the canceled Mass Effect Universe appearing online, and a petition for EA to reconsider its decision which has gained more than 325,000 signatures . A Canadian politician also started a government petition to save BioWare just last week.

articles.title: Colin Farrell Says 'There's a Conversation to Be Had' About The Penguin Season 2, Having Filmed Just 2 Scenes for The Batman Part II
articles.summary: Colin Farrell has confirmed he only appears in two scenes as the Penguin in The Batman Part II, but would love to play the character again in a potential Season 2 of the HBO show, insisting "there's a conversation to be had."
articles.body:
Colin Farrell has confirmed he only appears in two scenes as the Penguin in The Batman Part II , but would love to play the character again in a potential Season 2 of the HBO show, insisting "there's a conversation to be had."

Farrell is set to don the prosthetics once again as the Penguin in The Batman Part II, now due out February 18, 2028, having played the character first in The Batman and again in the well-received The Penguin HBO Max show.

In an interview on UK show This Morning to promote his upcoming film The Slightest Touch, Farrell was asked about playing the Penguin once again.

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

“I'd love to. I'd love to do a second season. There's a conversation to be had,” he replied. Farrell then talked about his role in The Batman Part II.

“So the Batman film, they're doing the sequel to The Batman, and I did two scenes in that. Just that. In and out. It was a bit tasty to do it. I was kind of moaning about the makeup again, but I do love the character and I'm very protective of the character. And there's definitely a conversation to be had about doing a second season.”

The Batman movies are from writer and director Matt Reeves, who recently drafted in Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh to help him finish principal photography on the sequel while he deals with a personal matter. Those Batman films, alongside The Penguin TV show, form part of what is called The Batman Epic Crime Saga , which is separate to James Gunn’s rebooted DC Universe.

Gunn’s plan was to introduce a Batman of his own with The Brave and the Bold, but after this week’s dramatic news about his and fellow DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran's exit from the company , the future of the DCU and indeed a third potential Batman movie from Matt Reeves is up in the air. New Warner Bros. owner Skydance has yet to outline its plans for DC movies and TV shows, with both Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow and Reeves’ The Batman Part II still down for release in theaters.

As for Farrell, in June he said he had read The Batman Part II script , which was written by Reeves and Mattson Tomlin, and loved it. Speaking to ScreenRant , Farrell described the script, and his involvement in the movie.

"I got to read from the first to last page and it's really magnificent,” he said. “I just think Matt Reeves is brilliant and he wrote, not only tonally, a really kind of dark and at times terrifying piece, and not only psychologically weighty and nuanced, but really feeling. It's a really... There's moments in it. It's full of feeling. I just think he wrote kind of a contemporary genre masterpiece, really. I'm only in two scenes, which is great because it means I can enjoy the rest of the film."

articles.title: Sony’s latest Pulse wireless headset packs planar magnetic drivers at a good price
articles.summary: We went hands-on with Sony’s $99 Pulse wireless headset, which has planar magnetic drivers and the ability to stream audio over Bluetooth and PlayStation Link.
articles.body: It’s tempting to seek out the do-everything wireless gaming headset with noise cancellation, phenomenal sound quality, multiplatform connectivity, swappable batteries — you name it. But if you just want the basics done well, Sony’s new $99.99 PlayStation Pulse headset is worth considering. It has very good sound and just enough extras, even if you use more gadgets than just your PlayStation 5. Inside the Pulse’s nondescript ear cup shells are custom planar magnetic drivers, which deliver clean, detailed sound whether you’re gaming, listening to music, or both. They aren’t bass-heavy or too shrill; their default equalizer is pleasing and punchy, though you can also tweak it in the PS5’s interface, like other Pulse headsets. They’re not Sony’s first audio gaming product to feature this type of high-end driver (the first was in 2023), but they are the most affordable at $99. [Product: Sony PlayStation Pulse wireless headset | The Pulse comes with either a white or black headband, with a soft-touch underside and a decent amount of give near the top of your head where it rests its weight. Thankfully, the headset is lightweight and offers size adjustments that go beyond what my large head requires for comfort. These are some of the only headphones I’ve used with ear cups that can rotate 180 degrees in either direction. Functionally, the Pulse stands out as a semi-affordable wireless headset that can stream audio from PlayStation Link (Sony’s low-latency, lossless wireless connection) and Bluetooth simultaneously. It includes a USB-C Link dongle that lets you pair it quickly with whatever you plug it into, whether it’s a PS5, PC, or Nintendo Switch 2. [Image: [Image: The headset’s ear cup controls include a dedicated Bluetooth button that, beyond pairing with another gadget, lets you pause or resume Bluetooth content (it can also answer or hang up calls). You can also control Bluetooth audio volume using the integrated volume rocker, but only when a device isn’t connected via PlayStation Link. In simultaneous audio mode, the rocker adjusts audio solely for the device connected via the Link dongle. If you have Sony’s PlayStation Portal, the Pulse can connect directly to the handheld without the Link dongle, just as Sony’s Pulse Elite and Explore can. It’s so convenient, and I hope Sony pushes for more devices that integrate the Link wireless technology in the future. [Image: I dig that its ear cups can be rotated to rest on my chest when I need a break. The Pulse isn’t the only headset that Sony has in the works. Its Pulse Edge wireless headset doesn’t have an exact launch date or price, but the company touts that it packs in twice as many magnets in its drivers (eight versus four), active noise cancellation, and a detachable boom mic that will likely provide better-sounding voice audio than the built-in mic in the standard Pulse. It will also include game / chat audio controls, a 3.5mm jack, and a carrying case. While the $99 Pulse is comparatively light on features, Sony’s focus on providing standout audio quality and comfort makes it worth seeking out if you have a PS5 and are on a strict budget for your next wireless headset.
